newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan president urged to probe disappearances.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan president urged to probe disappearances.

text.p: A pro-government Tamil party has urged Sri Lanka's president to intervene to stop alleged human rights abuses by the army in the Jaffna area recently captured from Tamil Tiger rebels, a party leader said on Saturday.

Joseph Pararajasingham, parliamentary leader of the Tamil United Liberation Front (TULF), wrote to President Chandrika Kumaratunga asking her to help implement in earnest the government's pledge to observe human rights.

An 18-year-old Tamil schoolgirl -- as well as her family who tried to locate her after she was arrested by the army -- have been missing in the northern Jaffna town of Kaithady for a week, he said in a letter to Kumaratunga, which was made available to journalists.

Pararajasingham, a lawmaker from Batticaloa district with many Tamil and Moslem voters, said the army denied arresting Krishanthy Kumarasamy, her mother, brother and a family friend although there were eyewitnesses.
"The denial of the army arresting any one of them causes alarm and suspicion that these four persons have disappeared while in custody of the army," the letter said.
He said there had been many cases of disappearances after arrests by security forces in Jaffna.

Predominantly Sinhalese government forces recaptured the Jaffna peninsula, 320 km (220 miles) north of Colombo, in April after a series of major offensives against the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels.
LTTE, fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in north and east of the country, had ruled Jaffna as a mini-state for almost a decade with their own administration, courts and police.
A military spokesman declined to comment on the letter but said a close relative of missing persons could lodge a complaint under strict procedures.

The letter said the army's denial followed allegations by human rights groups that extrajudicial executions, disappearances, torture and arbitary arrests continued to take place in Jaffna by security forces.

"Under the above circumstances, I would appreciate if your excellency order an impartial inquiry" into the arrest of the four and "give strict instructions to the security forces in Jaffna to adhere to your excellency's guidelines pertaining to arrest," it said.
The letter comes two weeks after the government approved a plan to allow Sri Lankans to appeal directly to a United Nations committee if they had any complaints of rights violations.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war between Tamil Tiger rebels and government troops, now in its 14th year.
